# Superseded-in-Place Documentation

When a decision is reversed, the document is not rewritten. A **dated SUPERSEDED banner** is stacked
on top of the original text, and the original stays underneath, readable.

In [[stickfps]] the clearest case is the art direction. Strict film-noir grayscale was a *mandatory
hard constraint* in three separate documents — `DESIGN_PROMPT.md` §3, `docs/DESIGN-BRIEF.md` §2 and
`docs/SRS.md` FR-9.3 — and was retired for full colour on 2026-07-24. All three still carry the
mandate, banner-stamped rather than deleted. The SRS's retired transport sections are handled the
same way: a prose note in constraint C2 rather than an edit to §1.2, §4.3, §4.4, §6.5 or the diagrams.

## What it buys

An auditable history in the working tree. A reader can see **what was once required and when it
stopped being required**, which a clean rewrite destroys. It is the documentation form of the same
instinct as [[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]], and it is why the reversal in
[[websocket-tcp-over-geckos-udp]] and [[render-over-fly-io]] can be reconstructed at all.

It also lowers the cost of reversing a decision. Rewriting three documents to change the art
direction is a task; adding three banners is not. Cheap reversals are worth something in themselves.

## What it costs

**Internal contradiction, permanently.** The document is now two documents interleaved, and a reader
who enters below the banner gets the retired answer with no warning. `docs/DESIGN-BRIEF.md` §7 still
reasons from a premise its own banner retired a hundred lines earlier:

> "since play is grayscale"
> — browser_game_stickfps/docs/DESIGN-BRIEF.md, 2026-07-25

Consumers downstream of the prose do not see the banner at all. `TASKS.md` still directs the
deployment at the retired host:

> "Backend to Fly.io (`flyctl launch`, PORT=9090, UDP enabled)"
> — browser_game_stickfps/TASKS.md, 2026-07-25

## The line between this and drift

They are easy to confuse and the difference is whether the reversal was **marked**. A banner over
stale text is superseded-in-place: the document knows. `EXPOSE 10000/udp` in the Dockerfile and the
four `.tooling` files still naming Geckos.io have no banner and no note — nobody knows, and the loop
that reads them treats them as current. That is [[documentation-drift]], and it is the failure this
pattern is a partial defence against, not a form of it.

The practice is only sound if the banner sits where the reader enters. Applied to a long document
read in sections, it degrades into drift with a disclaimer at the top.
